transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Thank you. Well, I'm here because I feel like I'm just always up and moving. Even on what's supposed to be a quiet day, I can't seem to settle down. I find myself bouncing from sorting out the garden club list, to grabbing my knitting bag, to looking through travel papers... and I do all that before I've really finished any one thing. It's just constant, and I figured it was time to talk to someone about it.
Has this constant need to be busy and jump between activities been a lifelong pattern for you, or is this a change from how you normally feel and act?

Well, I wouldn't say it's been my whole life, no. It's been especially noticeable for about a year and ten months now. That's right around the time I took on the extra coordinating work at the community center, along with all my other activities. Ever since then, this feeling has just been very obvious.
During this time, have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual to feel rested, without feeling tired the next day?
No, not at all. I still need my regular amount of sleep. If I don't get a good night's rest, I definitely feel tired the next day. So, no, I haven't noticed anything like that.

During this time, have you found yourself worrying excessively about various things—like your responsibilities or things that might go wrong—more than you feel you should, and having trouble controlling that worry?

No, I wouldn't say I worry excessively. I mean, I care about getting things done right for the community center and the garden club, but it's not like I'm sitting around anxious or agonizing over things going wrong. It's more just... I have a lot going on and I'm always moving between it all. But I don't feel overwhelmed by worry, no.
Thinking back to when you were a child or teenager, did you have similar struggles with restlessness, difficulty focusing, or jumping between activities before you were 12 years old?

Well, I know I just said the constant busyness is more recent, but... yes, thinking about it, I suppose I did have some of those struggles as a child. Even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright girl, but just very scattered. I was always losing my papers, and I had a bad habit of talking out of turn. I couldn't sit still, either—I'd just be wiggling around in my seat before I even finished my work. So, yes, I guess those kinds of things were happening back then, too.

Between your school years and the last couple of years, did you continue to notice these same kinds of restlessness and difficulty focusing, or was there a stretch of time where you felt more settled and didn't have these issues?

Well, looking back... I think it's always been there, really. I don't remember a time where I just felt completely settled. Even after I finished high school and got older, I was always the one jumping from one project to another, never quite finishing things. I've always had a hard time sitting through long meetings or just relaxing without feeling like I need to be doing something. So, no, there wasn't really a time where it went away. It's just kind of been a constant thing throughout my life.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out hypomania/mania (normal sleep need, no elevated mood) and GAD (no excessive uncontrollable worry). History confirms lifelong, continuous symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity since childhood, supporting ADHD as sole diagnosis.
